name: Rendered 3D objects and scenes

source.description: Five inspected references rely on real 3D rendering: clay-render isometric scenes, chrome objects with reflections, voxel cube fields, rotating point clouds and a dotted globe.

technique: Lit, shaded 3D geometry (materials, reflections, soft shadows, camera moves through space) gives products and systems physical presence that flat vector work cannot.
purpose: Show physical products, infrastructure or spatial systems; premium hero moments.
visual_behaviour: Objects turn, explode into parts or are flown through with a camera; materials respond to light (chrome reflections, matte clay shading); point clouds morph between volumes.
mechanics: Perspective camera paths, physically based or matcap materials, per-frame lighting; point clouds as projected 3D samples.

decomposition.timing: Camera moves of 2-6 s; object turns of 1-3 s.

failure_modes: Real-time WebGL in headless capture may stall or exceed the 1.5 GB render budget
Non-deterministic render loops break frame-accurate seeking
Recreating a specific product (a branded chip, device or logo object) without authorisation

implementation.approach: Not implemented. Preferred path: pre-render the 3D shot offline (Blender on the render host or external compute) to a short video, normalise with scripts/ingest-asset.sh and composite it under SVG/DOM with the approved hybrid-video-underlay effect. Cheap approximations for some cases are listed under capability.
implementation.notes: three.js is catalogued as 'proposed'; the algorithmic-art skill documents Blender usage.

requirements: 3D renderer with lighting and materials (WebGL/three.js or an offline renderer)
deterministic per-frame rendering driven by the timeline
GPU memory headroom inside the 1.5 GB render budget
additional_dependencies: three.js (catalogue: proposed) with a seek-driven render hook, or Blender for offline pre-renders

resources.gpu: high for WebGL in headless capture
resources.memory: unknown; must be benchmarked against the 1.5 GB ceiling

capability.native_option: None faithful: the DOM/SVG renderer has no lighting model.
capability.approximation: 2.5D: isometric SVG layers with flat shading (see isometric-exploded-view), CSS 3D transforms for tilted cards and carousels (css-3d-staging), and SVG point clouds projected from 3D coordinates for dotted globes or sphere-to-torus morphs (sampled into keyframes, no lighting). Loses materials, reflections and soft shadows.
capability.advanced_path: 1) Offline pre-render in Blender (EEVEE) at 720p into a short loop, ingest with scripts/ingest-asset.sh, composite with hybrid-video-underlay: proven pipeline, no runtime risk, cost is authoring time. 2) three.js with a seek-safe render hook (render the scene from timeline time inside a tween modifier) after a low-memory HyperFrames benchmark on the M2. Justified when a brief needs a physical product or hardware hero shot that 2.5D cannot carry.

additional_tooling.justification: No current brief requires it; the offline pre-render path needs no new runtime dependency and should be tried first.

limitations: Not available in the current runtime
Any 3D model of a real product needs rights clearance

priority.note: Seen in 5 of 14 references, but expensive; start with the pre-render path when a brief demands it.

provenance.observed: Clay-render isometric scenes of a facility, server racks and an exploded chip, explored with camera moves.
A voxel cube field and chrome knot and blob objects with reflections.
A chrome sphere with an orbiting ring in a dark space, reached by a camera push.
A dot grid becomes a rotating point-cloud sphere that morphs into a torus.
A glowing dotted globe horizon under a counter (approx., from overview spacing).

licensing_notes: Technique only. Reference objects include branded hardware and products; never model or reproduce them. Use original or licensed models.
